title: Pricey cart items
prompt: Merchandising wants to see which cart changes touch expensive products. Write `solve(cart_events)` so it returns `event_id`, `action`, `pricey_skus` (the skus of items with a `price` of 50.00 or more) and `any_bulk` (true when at least one item has a `qty` of more than 1).
rules: Keep one row per cart event, in any order. Keep duplicate rows.
An item counts as pricey when its unit `price` is 50.00 or more; quantity doesn't matter. Keep the pricey items' order. An item with a missing price isn't pricey.
With no pricey items, `pricey_skus` is an empty array. An event with no items has `any_bulk` false.
Return only `event_id`, `action`, `pricey_skus` and `any_bulk`, in that order.
hints: Two steps for `pricey_skus`: keep the right items with `F.filter`, then turn each into its sku with `F.transform`.
"At least one item" is `F.exists`. "50.00 or more" is `>=`.
`F.filter` returns an array, so its result can go straight into `F.transform`. Inside each lambda, `x["price"]` and `x["sku"]` reach the item's fields.
starter:
